**<sub><sub>![P0 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P0-red?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep OIDC federation behind the protected environment**

When this workflow template is installed, `parchwell-sweeper` becomes a second, no-reviewer federated subject for the same apply-capable Azure app. Restricting the workflow to a destroy command does not restrict the permissions of the issued token, so this broadens identity scope beyond the protected scenario environment and requires the repository's explicit approval-only P0 disposition.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Create the worker namespace before starting the watch**

On a fresh AKS cluster, this preflight binds the cluster but never creates the required `parchwell` namespace. No Terraform resource, chart template, or other Runner path creates it, so the subsequent `kubectl get pods -n parchwell` fails with `NotFound` before the first worker chart can be applied; create or apply the explicit namespace here as required by the runner contract.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for projected configuration before releasing the producer**

The runner patches the generated-values ConfigMap and later this admission ConfigMap, but never verifies that the running producer has observed the first update before exposing the permit. Mounted ConfigMap updates are only eventually projected and may be delayed by the kubelet sync/cache interval ([Kubernetes documentation](https://v1-35.docs.kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-pod-configmap/)); if the admission update becomes visible first, LoadGen hashes the stale `-pending` generated values and fails, and a slow start-line run can also leave too little of LoadGen's fixed 180-second admission deadline for the permit update to arrive.
